newsitem.title: USA: True Value, ServiStar create $4.5 billion co-operative.
newsitem.headline: True Value, ServiStar create $4.5 billion co-operative.

text.p: Cotter & Co., the largest wholesaler of hardware and related products to True Value stores, and ServiStar Coast to Coast Corp., the third largest wholesaler in the do-it-yourself market, agreed to merge, the companies said Tuesday.
The merger of the two co-operatives will create a new co-operative, TruServ Corp., which is expected to have initial annual sales of about $4.5 billion, they said.
The goal of the combined entity is to preserve the future growth of the nearly 10,500 independent retailer members who will belong to the co-operative, they said in a statement.
Cotter and ServiStar said they expected to realize significant cost savings from consolidating warehouse facilities and delivering products on common trucks.
A plan is being developed to improve efficiencies of the new company. Some jobs will be lost, others will be moved, a spokesman for the co-operatives said.
Members of the two predecessor co-operatives will exchange common and preferred stock in their co-operatives for stock in the new co-operative on a dollar-for-dollar basis.

"By consolidating our operations we expect to give our owner/members better prices, better services and long term strength in the wholesale industry," said Dan Cotter, president and chief executive officer of Cotter & Co. Dan Cotter has been designated chairman and chief executive officer of TruServ.
Paul Pentz, president and chief executive officer of ServiStar, has been designated president, chief operating officer, and a director of TruServ.

Directors of Cotter and ServStar approved the proposed merger on Dec. 9. Proxy materials will be mailed to members of both co-operatives as soon as regulatory requirements are met, tentatively set for mid-January, 1997. Merger votes are due by March 1, 1997.
Under the proposed plan, TruServ's headquarters will be located at Cotter & Co's offices near Chicago.
"This merger should gain more competitive prices for independent retailers, and consequently for consumers," said Cotter in a statement.
True Value has 6,000 stores in 51 countries and ServiStar has 4,500 stores in 44 countries.
